newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $63 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $63 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was extremely slow at $63.00 per cwt, unchanged from this week's sales, feedlot sources said.

About 200 steers that will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas following weekly sales near 95,000 head. There were no reported sales in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area following weekly movement near 104,500 head.
This week's trade sold out most showlists as packers bought the cattle needed to get through next week's Independence Day holiday-shortened work week, the feedlot sources said.
Sales this week at $63.00 were down $1.00 from last week amid lower CME live cattle futures, weak beef prices and a need by feedlots to remain current, the sources said.
Feedlots need to stay current as they head into July becuase of outlooks calling for expanded market-ready cattle supplies, they said.
Packers lowered beef prices this week because of continued large beef production and their ability to buy cattle at less money than a week ago, the sources said.
